review_note: Difficult second-half markets, a 15.6% decline in underlying operating profit and an active centralisation and cost-reduction programme with £1.8m forecast cash cost indicated material pressure; gross margin improved 100bps, operating cash generation rose to £13.2m and net debt fell £3.3m, providing strong but incomplete offsets. The disclosed restructuring was already public at cutoff and is excluded as a future target event.

Supply disruption, broad inflation, delayed project conversion and uneven Services performance remained specific pressure, while earlier cost-base and warehouse restructuring was already public; gross margin improved 100bps and profit recovered strongly, but an £8.7m working-capital build absorbed trading cash and increased net debt, leaving strong yet qualified contrary evidence.

Market headwinds, weaker OEM demand, lower revenue and underlying operating profit, a statutory loss, organisational and sales restructuring, and quantified headcount reductions showed substantial intervention pressure. Group gross margin improved 111bps and operating cash generation rose, while net debt reduced year on year but remained above management expectations; these operational improvements supplied meaningful, not decisive, contrary evidence. The disclosed 2023 actions are excluded as future target events.

The creation of B2B and B2C divisions was growth-oriented integration rather than evidence of unresolved operating distress. Revenue rose 24%, adjusted EBITDA 29%, operating cash conversion reached 90% and interest cover remained strong; acquisition-funded adjusted net debt increased to £9.2m but gearing of 1.41x was described as prudent, leaving multiple strong quantified contrary indicators.
